name: Mamata Banerjee
role: Indian politician; Chief Minister of West Bengal 2011-2026 and founder-leader of the Trinamool Congress; also Union Railway Minister (1999-2000, 2009-2011)
summary: Banerjee is a populist, welfare-oriented politician of the Bengali centre-left who rose by opposing forcible farmland acquisition at Singur and Nandigram. She backs wide cash-transfer and health schemes, legal crop price guarantees and a strong federal role for states, and opposes the CAA, NRC and a Uniform Civil Code while stressing communal harmony. She courts industry, favours rapid growth and tough punishment for rape, and accuses the BJP-led Centre of undermining federalism and democracy.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The 2024 manifesto, issued over her signed appeal, says her government 'pioneered universal healthcare' and achieved universal health coverage through Swasthya Sathi (free care up to Rs 5 lakh a year), and pledges a national scheme with Rs 10 lakh cover; the 2026 manifesto adds doorstep health camps.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Her 2024 manifesto promises a national minimum wage of Rs 400 a day for all workers, and the 2026 manifesto lifts the tea-garden minimum wage from Rs 250 to Rs 300 a day.

public-ownership.rationale: As Railway Minister she made clear the railways would not be privatised (as reported in 2010), and the 2024 manifesto she fronted condemns the privatisation of PSUs such as LIC for lost revenue and jobs; her railway budgets also invited private partners through PPP.

notes: Wikipedia (June-August 2026) says her chief ministership ended when the assembly was dissolved on 7 May 2026 after the TMC lost the 2026 election and she lost Bhabanipur; she leads the Mamata All India Trinamool Congress after a 2026 split. She is alive, so living is true. Evidence rests mostly on the two TMC manifestos she fronted (2024 Lok Sabha, 2026 assembly, both read in full), her 2011 railway budget speech, and press-reported quotations; manifesto lines are party programme that she signed, so most are medium. Her best-known views on immigration changed over time (2005 versus 2018 onward) and are left at 0. Several topics (abortion, same-sex marriage, gender identity, language policy, trade, climate) had no direct statement found and stay null. The 2024 manifesto original on aitcofficial.org returned 404; the Wayback copy was used. Searches for her Singur-era speeches found only press paraphrases.
